mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.3 percentage points in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last two months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity and related sectors.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where housing starts increased over the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where industrial production increased by more than 1% in the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% within the last month signals a weakening demand, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending slows and economic growth decelerates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where real personal consumption expenditures decreased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the cost of capital rises and inflation erodes purchasing power.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% in the last six months signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where real GDP increased by more than 2% in the previous six months.
